comparator.sourceNotes: The current official programme page confirms a language-centred Italian Studies degree: students develop spoken and written Italian, study Italian linguistics, literature, culture and society, and are prepared to write the thesis in Italian. The latest complete official study guide supplies a coherent 180-EC structure: fixed 60-EC first and second years, followed by 20 EC of Italian subject work, 30 EC of genuine elective space and a 10-EC thesis in Year 3. The first two listed monographic options are instantiated neutrally; the open elective space is not populated with invented subjects.

exception.reason: Leiden Italian Language and Culture is organized around cumulative Italian proficiency and sustained Italian-language study of linguistics, literature, culture and society. Its compulsory sequence progresses from Lingua italiana Ia/Ib/Ic through IIa/IIb, while subject courses cover Italian phonology, morphology, syntax, language history and variation, medieval through contemporary literature, and Italian cultural history. The thesis may be written in Italian. UCR offers strong adjacent humanities courses, including one focused on Renaissance Italy, but no Italian language instruction, no Italian-language source-analysis sequence and no Italian linguistics. A 24-course UCR pathway in general European history, literature, film, communication and art would therefore replace the degree's continuous language-and-area core rather than provide a defensible comparator.
exception.curriculumContext: The latest complete official programme accounts for exactly 180 EC: fixed 60-EC first and second years, followed by 20 EC of Italian subject work, 30 EC of genuine free choice and a 10-EC BA thesis in Year 3. Year 1 contains 20 EC of Italian proficiency alongside Italian literature, culture, linguistics and Romance linguistics. Year 2 contains 20 further EC of Italian proficiency plus Italian poetry, contemporary language, present-day Italy, Dante, modern literature, history of Italian and a subject research paper. Year 3 continues Italian literature and linguistics through fixed and monographic courses before the thesis. The official programme outcomes target high Italian proficiency, analysis of Italian phonology, morphology, syntax and semantics, recognition of historical, geographical and sociolinguistic variants, and knowledge of Italian literary and cultural history.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 records in the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx (SHA-256 7bf6c2ae9de0837086ec741c27bd94ed7e85dff2d25bde619ecd50cc4d685879), including names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned availability. MCCHEAM212 Renaissance Italy & Global Mediterranean directly addresses Renaissance Italian art and Mediterranean connections, while MCCHEAM111 Introduction to Western Art History supplies broader European art-historical context. MCCLITR111 Introduction to Literary Studies, MCCLITR112 Great Literary Works, MCCLITR311 Film & Text and MCCLITR312 Perspectives on Literary Meaning provide literary methods; MCCMEDI111 Introduction to Film & Media supports film analysis; GOSHIST111 Modern History provides European historical context. MCCCOMM211 Style & Meaning examines linguistic choices in texts and HCBCOGN312 Psycholinguistics studies language processing, but neither teaches Italian. The workbook contains no Italian course, no cumulative Italian grammar, vocabulary, listening, speaking, reading or writing sequence, no study of Italian phonology, morphology, syntax, dialects or minority languages, no sustained Italian-language literary curriculum, and no Italian-language thesis preparation. The adjacent Renaissance, history, literature, film and language-science courses cannot substitute for the compulsory Italian-language disciplinary spine.
